key_insight: A logarithmic correction with exponent 1/3 enables a constant, positive energy flux toward small scales in 2D quantum-fluid wave turbulence, where the naive power law instead describes thermal equilibrium.
engineering_relevance: The corrected spectrum can guide interpretation and numerical modeling of energy transfer in two-dimensional Bose gases.
method: Derive the logarithmic correction through an asymptotic expansion of the wave-kinetic collision integral.
Set the logarithmic upper cutoff using the small-scale dissipation scale.
Regularize the marginal infrared divergence at the forcing scale to estimate the spectral prefactor.
evidence_signal: Gross-Pitaevskii and wave-kinetic simulations support the predicted spectral shape, whose finite-range appearance may explain steep spectra observed in 2D Bose gas experiments.
watch_item: The prefactor estimate assumes asymptotically well-separated forcing and dissipation scales, so finite-scale applications require caution.
paper_title: Energy cascade spectrum in wave turbulence of a two-dimensional quantum fluid
